transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I guess… I’ve been feeling like I can’t really shut off. I finish one thing at school or at home and I’m already moving to the next. It’s like I’m running on a motor most of the time.
Have you been having times when you feel unusually happy or high?
Not really… I mean, I don’t think so. I get keyed up, sure, but not like unusually happy or high.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal things, but not… not for no reason, I guess.
Do you often have trouble paying attention, even when you’re trying to focus?
I’m not sure. I mean… I can usually pay attention when I need to. It’s more that I get restless, I guess.
Were you this restless when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. My mother used to say I was always up out of my chair in elementary school, talking or jumping in before the teacher even finished giving directions. She’d joke that I was “teaching the class from my seat.” So… it wasn’t just something that started later.

patient.answer: Yeah… I think so. My mother used to say I was always up out of my chair in elementary school, talking or jumping in before the teacher even finished giving directions. She’d joke that I was “teaching the class from my seat.” So… it wasn’t just something that started later.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a hyperactive/impulsive ADHD presentation with longstanding symptoms since childhood, including being constantly 'on the go,' frequently leaving the seat in elementary school, excessive talking, and blurting out before directions were finished. There is no evidence here for manic mood elevation or excessive generalized worry, and inattentive symptoms were not prominent. Given the provided candidate set, F90.0 is the best-fitting diagnosis.
